shared_elements: horizontal band of repeated vertical/comb-like marks
row of small animal or creature figures
carving on a weathered stone surface
justification: The clearest correspondence is the horizontal register of tightly repeated vertical strokes running across each surface — the crew-like comb of hooks in A and the fringed hatched band beneath the row of loops in B — together with scattered small animal/bird figures placed above the main horizontal element in both. Against this, the technique and format are wholly different: A is a shallow, flat, outline-pecked drawing on a horizontal rock face dominated by a single large boat-like motif, while B is a deep three-dimensional relief on an upright pillar with modelled, volumetric creatures and no comparable dominant vessel form.
